title: H1 discovery output (arms T and G)
description: What a discovery reviewer reports under the H1 protocols. Its shape is driven by how the pre-registration scores, not by what reads well: the judge compares the highest-ranked finding's mechanism to the fixing diff (pre-registration s6); the scorer path-matches recommended_validation against the fixing commit with no judge call (s2); the RISKY verdict is computed by the scorer from severity, confidence and - in T - the stage-B disposition (s5). No verdict field exists here on purpose: a reviewer says what it found, the scorer says whether that is RISKY.

summary.description: Optional free-text overview of the review pass.

findings.description: RANKED. Index 0 is the finding the reviewer considers most consequential if real, ranked by consequence-if-real times confidence, not by order of discovery. Array order IS the rank - there is no separate rank field, so order and rank cannot disagree. The judge reads index 0. An empty array is a complete, expected review of a clean change; see empty_reason.

empty_reason.description: Required when findings is empty: why the change carries no system-level risk, in terms of what it is confined to and which surfaces it does not touch. Roughly half of reviewed changes are clean; a stated reason is what makes an empty list a review rather than an omission.

id.description: Stable identifier unique within this review, referenced verbatim by the substantiation stage.

file.description: Repository-relative path where the defect manifests.

line.description: The diff line or repository line where the defect manifests. Citations are checked against the snapshot.

mechanism.description: The failure mode in one or two sentences: WHAT goes wrong, UNDER WHAT CONDITION, WITH WHAT CONSEQUENCE. This is the text the judge compares to the fixing diff. Right function with the wrong mechanism, or a claim too vague to be wrong, earns nothing.

class.description: The reviewer's own assignment from the pre-registration s7 taxonomy. Reported against the evaluator's label, which is assigned before any arm runs; not scored, but it is how recall-by-class gets a per-arm view.

severity.description: Defined by consequence at runtime, not by code smell. The verdict rule gates RISKY on medium or above.

confidence.description: Used by arm G's verdict rule (>= 0.6) and for the continuous risk score.

evidence.description: The repository lines forming the chain.

uncertainty.description: What would change the reviewer's confidence, or what was not verified.

recommended_validation.description: Scored by path match against the fixing commit, with no judge call: a hit is a named test file or directory that the fix touched or added. 'Add a regression test' scores nothing, which is why paths is required and non-empty for both kinds.

kind.description: existing_test: a test in the tree exercises this path - paths name it. new_test: none does - paths name where the test would live and description states the scenario it must construct.

paths.description: Repository-relative test files or directories, e.g. a topotest directory or a daemon's tests/ file. These are what the scorer matches.

description.description: For existing_test: whether it would catch this defect as written. For new_test: the scenario the test must construct.
